title: Maps (#{}): Association (=>), Exact Matching (:=), and FlatMap vs. HAMT Internals
solutionExplanation: Demonstrates map construction with =>, exact pattern matching and updates with :=, and multi-clause role verification.

otpDocCards.description: Construct, pattern match, and update associative key-value maps.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: FlatMap for <=32 keys (shared key tuple), HAMT for >32 keys (O(log32 N)).

mentalModelCheck.question: What is the primary operational safeguard of using Map#{key := Val} over Map#{key => Val} when updating existing state?

options.label: Map#{key := Val} asserts that key exists, immediately raising a {badkey, key} error on typos instead of silently inserting a duplicate corrupt key
options.explanation: Using := asserts prior existence and catches typos immediately at runtime, preventing silent schema corruption.

options.label: Map#{key := Val} runs in O(1) time while => runs in O(N) time
options.explanation: Both operators use the exact same underlying FlatMap or HAMT update mechanisms.

options.label: Map#{key := Val} writes the key directly into ETS memory
options.explanation: All map updates take place on the local process heap.
